newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Two foreign reporters among those detained in Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Two foreign reporters among those detained in Malaysia.

text.p: Malaysian police detained two foreign reporters along with local and foreign activists on Saturday at a controversial conference on East Timor which was broken up by youths allied with the ruling government coalition, witnesses said.

Asiaweek's correspondent in Kuala Lumpur Roger Mitton and the Singapore-based correspondent for Australia Broadcasting Corporation Catherine McGrath were taken away in a police truck along with the activists, witnesses said.

They were taken out of a central Kuala Lumpur hotel along with about 30 Malaysian activists who were trying to hold a conference on East Timor, which Indonesia invaded in 1975 and annexed the following year.
Police declined comment as to why the two foreign reporters or the activists were being detained.

A youth group allied to Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's ruling coalition broke up the meeting with boisterous chanting and singing of patriotic songs, saying the conference would damage Malaysia's ties with neighbouring Indonesia. About 10 members of the youth group have also been detained, police said.
